title: Enterprise Account Manager
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

Lyft Business is changing the way companies, brands and organizations leverage the Lyft platform to redefine the way they operate and move people around. We are solving big problems, and meeting the needs of our clients and the people they care about in a whole new way. We realize that the world has changed so much recently, and that the needs of our customers and how they envision transportation is changing too. Our work is fun, challenging and rewarding and we are looking for customer and growth-focused team members passionate about solving problems and delighting our customers. 

As an Account Manager, you’ll help our clients understand the power of Lyft Business. You will build and manage a named account list of large organizations in the US, ensuring that they leverage Lyft’s products for any transportation objective they have. We’re building the next great transportation platform, and we need world-class talent and candidates that aren’t afraid to try new things and think outside the box to build new business. 

Responsibilities:

  • Own the customer relationship with enterprise grade partners as their primary representative to Lyft for all their business related transportation needs 
  • Partner with Fortune 500 companies, to design, sell and implement custom transportation solutions for their respective passengers that include employees (essential and non), recruits, VIPs, guests, subscribers, etc
  • Identify and generate additional revenue streams within existing accounts, including up-sells and cross-sells; selling across commuter benefits, events, employee perks, concierge, and corporate travel use cases to exceed revenue targets
  • Generate and maintain an active pipeline with meticulous attention to opportunity staging, close dates, revenue forecasts, and deal documentation
  • Constantly ‘sell’ Lyft to stakeholders within client organizations, seeking to uplevel your decision maker contacts, and ensure a wide list of contacts within various segments of your customer’s organization
  • Work with internal cross-functional partners to represent the voice of your clients with Product, Engineering, Sales Operations, Legal, Marketing, etc. 
  • Lead and own recurring check-ins and scalable touch points (including formal QBRs) with clients. 
  • Scalably address roadblocks, tackle challenges, highlight success, and communicate account ‘health’ updates and best practices
  • Collaborate with Marketing team in order to develop strong and scalable ‘go to market’ collateral and campaigns to execute within your clients’ organizations
  • Operate in a proactive and entrepreneurial manner. There’s no wrong way to evangelize Lyft within your customer set. You’ll be given the autonomy and resources to plan your own path to success, with the expectation to execute quickly. 
  • Have comfort in operating in the gray. Programs will fail as others succeed. Take note of what works, and help build our playbook for new B2B transportation use cases for Lyft.
  • Fully understand all of Lyft Business’ products and services, keeping abreast of product changes and how they may impact your customers or lead to increased usage.

Experience:

  • 4+ years of experience in a customer-facing role (Sales, Customer Success, Business Development experience preferred from any field)

title: Associate Counsel, Employment
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

Lyft is looking for a bright, pragmatic, and self-motivated employment attorney with 4+ years of employment counseling and litigation experience to join our growing global Legal team. The ideal candidate will leverage their prior law firm and/or in-house experience to provide thoughtful, timely, practical and business-minded legal advice primarily to the professionals on Lyft’s Employee Relations and People teams across the globe. You must have experience litigating and/or counseling on compliance with federal and state anti-discrimination/harassment/retaliation laws, preferably including analysis of issues under California law. Prior in-house or seconded technology company experience is preferred but not required. The successful candidate will be an entrepreneurial and resourceful self-starter, comfortable working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, excellent at building strong relationships and interested in learning more about supporting a global workforce.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide pragmatic day-to-day employment advice and counseling on a broad range of employment issues in order to balance business impact and legal risk including HR practices, performance management, terminations, leaves of absence, investigations, and employee accommodations.
  • Investigate pre-litigation and litigation matters.  Develop and implement strategies for early resolution (as appropriate) and work with outside counsel as appropriate.
  • Provide guidance and Interpret policies and procedures, incorporating knowledge of state and federal employment laws (e.g., FMLA, ADA, FLSA, NLRA, and Title VII and equivalent state and international laws).
  • Provide legal counsel and support to a global workforce.
  • Partner closely with Lyft’s Employee Relations and People team professionals on employee complaints and investigations, performance management, and accommodations.
  • Collaborate with other members of the Employment Legal Team and People Team to develop strong processes to ensure compliance with applicable state, federal and local laws.
  • Develop and deliver training to managers and employees -- candidates must be comfortable with public speaking.
  • Monitor important developments in employment law in jurisdictions across the country and internationally, striving to spot trends in their infancy.
  • Work and build trust with cross-functional partners from teams across the Legal Department and the Company.
  • Travel from time-to-time as necessary to service internal clients; develop cross-office relationships; and attend legal proceedings/negotiations.\

Experience:

  • 4+ years practicing employment law at a leading law firm and/or in-house, with experience and/or interest in advice and counseling
  • Prior in-house experience and expertise supporting a global workforce is a plus but not required.
  • Active and in good standing with a State Bar and eligible to practice in the relevant jurisdiction where you are located.

descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

Our Client Infrastructure team is dedicated to building software that addresses challenges at a large scale, ensuring that our mobile applications are stable, scalable, and efficient.

As a Mobile Engineer on the Mobile Foundations team, you will create and maintain foundational systems that all Lyft mobile engineers rely on, enabling teams across Lyft to deliver rich experiences that connect people and places. You will build scalable infrastructure, helping developers move fast and innovate, while ensuring Lyft's mobile developer experience remains at the forefront. Your work will have a multiplicative effect across Engineering and contribute directly to Lyft's overall stability.

Our apps are used by millions of people, and we take great pride in our work, which means adhering to excellent development practices, careful code architecture, and an organization built around rapid releases. Our codebase is written entirely in Swift, utilizing modern design patterns and coding standards. We rely on third-party libraries and actively contribute back to the community, including the Swift language itself.

Who are you:

  • You are an enthusiastic and experienced mobile developer looking to use your engineering skills to improve developers’ ability to ship new features quickly.
  • You get excited about new Swift features and compile improvements.
  • You find delight in building the foundations and frameworks to accelerate the development of others, hiding away the complexities of the system.
  • You are a diplomat who looks at the landscape and aligns engineers from different teams around a common pattern.
  • You are excited about scaling millions of lines of Swift code to hundreds of mobile developers.

  • Support iOS engineers from across the organization as they use the tools we build and leverage these interactions to improve our roadmaps and offerings.
  • Bring new ideas to the table that aim to ease developer friction and keep our codebase joyful to develop in while continuously improving the codebase through refactoring.
  • Stay current with iOS development and contribute to open-source projects like the Mobile Native Foundation and Hammer.

Experience:

  • Code Quality: Experienced in delivering high-quality code.

title: Marketing Technology Lead
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

We are hiring a Marketing Technology Lead to own Lyft's B2B marketing technology stack, spanning marketing automation, content and web, lead routing, data enrichment, and attribution. As the senior technical owner of that stack, you will lead solution design, own the architecture and data model that carry a lead from first touch through to a qualified opportunity, and partner with Marketing Operations, Sales Operations, Sales Technology, Privacy, Legal, and Data to translate business needs into durable, scalable systems. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who knows B2B marketing operations, can build the systems that run them, and is looking for ways to bring AI into how the stack works, not just what it produces.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the senior technical owner of the B2B marketing technology stack, from solution design through delivery, adoption, and ongoing support.
  • Lead requirements gathering with Marketing Operations, Sales Operations, Sales Technology, and Data partners, and translate them into functional and technical designs.
  • Remain hands-on, configuring and extending the marketing automation platform (HubSpot) across workflows, forms, lead scoring, and custom objects, and building the integrations that connect the stack.
  • Own the marketing technology roadmap and architecture, including the lead and account data model, enrichment and routing logic, and integrations with the CRM, data platform, web, and advertising systems.
  • Own the tracking and instrumentation layer, including tag management, site and campaign tracking, and the data capture behind attribution.
  • Own the lead lifecycle systems, partnering with Sales Operations and Sales Technology on lead identity, deduplication, scoring, routing, MQL and SQL definitions, and funnel stage integrity.
  • Identify where AI can improve the stack, from lead scoring and routing to content and campaign workflows, and lead the evaluation, adoption, and rollout of those capabilities.
  • Assess the stack against target state and introduce new tools as the marketing motion matures.
  • Set the technical standard through design review and documentation that accounts for failure states, scalability, and supportability.
  • Maintain platform reliability by monitoring performance and email deliverability, supporting incident resolution, leading postmortems, and driving automation.
  • Own governance and controls for marketing data, including consent and subscription management, email and privacy compliance, data quality, and change management.
  • Own the marketing tool portfolio and budget, from evaluation and selection through procurement, contracting, and renewals, partnering with Procurement, Legal, and Security.
  • Serve as the technical expert and escalation point, and deliver technical enablement to partner teams.
  • Partner with marketing leaders on prioritization, mentor the engineers and contractors supporting the stack, and support hiring.
  • Communicate marketing technology strategy, roadmap, and vision to partner teams, and give senior leadership decision-ready updates on progress, risks, and tradeoffs.

Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 7+ years of experience in a marketing technology, marketing operations engineering, or business systems role, including 3+ years leading solution design and delivery.

  • Hands-on depth in at least two platform categories beyond marketing automation, such as content management, lead routing, data enrichment, ABM, analytics, or attribution.
  • 3+ years hands-on in Salesforce or an equivalent CRM, and 3 or more delivered integrations to systems such as a data warehouse or CMS using REST APIs, webhooks, or middleware.
  • Hands-on experience with tag management and web or campaign tracking instrumentation.
  • Led end-to-end delivery of at least 2 large, cross-functional marketing technology programs, including one platform implementation or migration.
  • Experience providing technical direction to engineers, contractors, or implementation partners.

  • Proven ability to communicate technical direction and tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders, and present roadmap and status to senior leadership.
  • Experience with marketing data quality, consent and subscription management, and email and privacy compliance (CAN-SPAM, CASL, GDPR, or equivalent) is highly desirable.

title: Senior Business Systems Lead, Payroll & Time (Dayforce)
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect, cultivating an inclusive environment where all team members can thrive.

As the Business Systems Lead for Payroll & Time, you will lead Lyft's global migration onto Dayforce following recent acquisitions. Sitting within People Technology in Corporate Engineering and IT (CEIT), you'll join Lyft's Dayforce program at a formative moment: the initial rollout spans 12–15 countries over two-plus years, and you're joining early enough to directly shape how implementation, governance, and vendor management get done — not inherit a playbook someone else already wrote.

You'll be backed by a mature, experienced Payroll Operations team who bring deep subject-matter expertise, while you own the technical and functional side: driving requirements, directing our systems integrator, and building the governance and vendor management model you'll run long-term as the platform's product/service owner.

Sitting within People Technology in CEIT, you will drive requirements, make key functional decisions, and partner closely with Payroll Operations, HR, Legal, and Finance. You'll lead vendor delivery to ensure accurate, compliant payroll and time tracking across each migration wave, then own platform governance and vendor management long-term once the program stabilizes.

We're looking for someone who can act as the translation layer between operations, executives, and technical teams — equally comfortable explaining payroll concepts to engineers and system constraints to business stakeholders.

Responsibilities:

Own Requirements and Direct the Implementation Partner

  • Serve as the internal functional owner for the Dayforce payroll and time migration, driving requirements and directing the systems integrator partner.
  • Translate payroll policy, collective bargaining terms, and statutory requirements — as defined by Payroll Operations and Legal — into actionable technical specifications.
  • Validate vendor configurations against country-specific rules, with joint sign-off alongside Payroll Operations, before go-live.
  • Act as the primary functional escalation point, facilitating trade-off decisions between Payroll Ops, Legal, and vendor teams — owning the technical trade-off while deferring to Payroll Ops/Legal on compliance interpretation.
  • Partner with Program Management to identify and mitigate risks across migration waves.

Drive Migration Waves End-to-End

  • Scope requirements with cross-functional stakeholders ahead of each phased migration wave across the 12–15 country initial program.
  • Lead parallel testing and payroll validation cycles to verify system logic against live pay rules prior to cutover.
  • Manage cutover and hypercare support, serving as the technical escalation point until system stabilization.
  • Own integration architecture between Dayforce and upstream/downstream systems — including Workday, Oracle ERP, and middleware platforms (Boomi preferred) — ensuring resilient, well-governed data flows.
  • Align migration schedules with Workday and Oracle ERP initiatives to prevent deployment conflicts.

Own Steady-State Configuration and Continuous Improvement

  • Assume direct functional ownership of Dayforce payroll and time configuration post-implementation, as the platform's long-term product/service owner.
  • Establish and run governance frameworks and formal vendor management practices — contract oversight, SLA management, escalation processes — that outlast the initial implementation.
  • Maintain system documentation and runbooks to keep governance transparent and auditable.
  • Evaluate new vendor releases, system updates, and regulatory changes — partnering with Payroll Ops and Legal on interpretation — to proactively plan platform updates.
  • Ensure system configuration is built and maintained to the wage-and-hour, statutory pay, and data privacy requirements defined by Payroll Operations and Legal.
  • Streamline operations by automating manual payroll and time-tracking workarounds.
  • Support future expansion into scheduling configuration and provide system evidence for internal and external payroll audits.

Experience:

Required Qualifications

  • 6+ years of functional payroll and time tracking systems experience, with strong hands-on configuration expertise in Ceridian Dayforce.
  • Experience establishing governance frameworks and formal vendor management practices (contract oversight, SLA management, escalation processes) as a product or service owner — not solely as a project-based implementer.
  • Hands-on experience with middleware/integration architecture connecting payroll and time systems to upstream HCM and downstream ERP/finance systems; Boomi experience strongly preferred.
  • Proven track record as an internal functional owner managing system integrator delivery and holding vendors formally accountable.
  • Deep domain expertise in core payroll: earnings, deductions, tax setup, accruals, overtime, and multi-country/multi-state compliance.
  • Strong payroll literacy with a demonstrated ability to translate between payroll/operations terminology and technical/systems language — for both practitioner and executive audiences.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate business policy, legal, and collective bargaining agreements into system requirements.
  • Strong root-cause troubleshooting skills across complex payroll and time tracking scenarios.
  • Experience leading system strategy across multi-country, multi-phase transformation programs.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, capable of bridging technical detail with business and executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading global payroll transformations or M&A integrations with third-party implementation partners — international/cross-border experience strongly preferred.
  • Familiarity with in-country payroll providers (e.g., TMF, IRIS, Paylocity) used during transitional phases.
  • Hands-on experience with Dayforce time tracking and scheduling modules.
  • Understanding of Workday HCM and enterprise HRIS/ERP integration patterns.
  • Knowledge of payroll compliance across the specific countries in scope for this program.
  • Exposure to HR integration and automation platforms (e.g., Workato).
  • Prior experience operating in high-growth technology environments or navigating active M&A integrations.

title: Director, Trust & Safety
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive. Safety is fundamental to the Lyft experience and to the trust riders, drivers, and our broader communities place in our platform. Lyft’s Safety and Customer Care team works through product, technology, data, policy, and operations to prevent harm before it happens, respond compassionately when it does, and continuously learn from every incident in efforts to make Lyft the safest way to get around. 

We are looking for an experienced safety leader with deep Trust & Safety experience  to help turn Lyft’s Trust & Safety strategy into impact at scale, with the final shape of this role informed by the strengths of the leader we bring on. This is a highly visible leadership role within Lyft’s Safety & Customer Care organization. You will report to the Senior Director and General Manager of Trust & Safety and sit on the Trust & Safety leadership team. You will additionally partner deeply with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Research & Design, Legal, Compliance, Risk, Communications, Finance, and other teams across Lyft.

The ideal candidate is an exceptional operator and people leader with Trust & Safety expertise, strong strategic judgment, and a track record of leading complex, high-stakes Trust & Safety organizations at scale. You can move fluidly between setting strategy with senior executives, developing leaders, overseeing large global operations and budgets, and diving into an emerging safety issue when the situation demands it.

Responsibilities

Lead Global Safety Compliance & Risk

  • Oversee Lyft’s global safety compliance, transparency, and risk functions, supporting strong functional leaders and individual contributors on your team and strengthening capabilities as Lyft scales globally.
  • Set direction across compliance readiness, safety transparency reporting, and risk assessment, ensuring strong governance and execution.
  • Partner with Legal, Regulatory Compliance, and business leaders to anticipate emerging requirements and risks across markets, products, and business models.
  • Ensure material risks, dependencies, and gaps are surfaced early, with clear ownership and senior-level visibility.

Lead Trust & Safety Business Enablement

  • Guide the functions that turn Trust & Safety strategy and policy into scalable execution across the business.
  • Ensure teams are aligned around clear priorities, ownership, and outcomes while empowering functional leaders to drive execution.
  • Strengthen the playbooks, operating mechanisms, and cross-functional connections needed to safely launch new products, features, markets, and experiences.
  • Help evolve Lyft’s Trust & Safety operating model as the business grows in scale and complexity.

Lead Trust & Safety Partnerships

  • Set the Trust & Safety strategy for strategic partners, acquisitions, and businesses joining Lyft’s expanding global ecosystem.
  • Support partnership leaders in building scalable approaches across different products, markets, operating models, regulatory environments, and risk profiles.
  • Ensure partners are effectively integrated into Lyft’s safety ecosystem, with clear standards, ownership, governance, and escalation paths.
  • Surface partnership risks and readiness early, enabling Lyft to grow and integrate new businesses safely.

Drive the Operating Rhythm

  • Help translate strategy into priorities, operating plans, resource decisions, and measurable outcomes.
  • Drive the organization’s planning, prioritization, goal-setting, and business review rhythms, ensuring clear decisions, accountability, and follow-through.
  • Support the General Manager of Trust & Safety with Lyft-wide and executive efforts, including strategic planning, Board and executive preparation, and cross-functional initiatives requiring senior-level coordination.
  • Distill complex issues into clear, decision-ready narratives and recommendations for executives and cross-functional leaders.

Build and Lead Exceptional Teams

  • Lead talented individual contributors and people managers.
  • Build an organization with clear accountability, strong decision-making, high standards, and the ability to operate effectively through ambiguity and change.
  • Develop leaders who independently own large, complex areas while maintaining strong alignment across the broader Trust & Safety organization.
  • Create an environment where teams combine urgency with sound judgment, challenge assumptions constructively, learn from mistakes, and are grounded in the experiences of riders and drivers. 

Experience

  • 10+ years of relevant professional experience, with significant experience in Trust & Safety, safety, risk, integrity, customer operations, platform operations, or another closely related field.
  • Deep, direct experience leading at least two Trust & Safety functions (e.g. product and policy; policy and operations; operations and programs) at scale is required. 
  • Experience leading Trust & Safety at a scaled consumer technology, marketplace, mobility, social, sharing-economy, or other platform business.
  • 5+ years of significant people leadership experience, including demonstrated success managing individual contributors, managers or senior leaders, and leaders of leaders.
  • Demonstrated experience owning significant budgets and making strategic tradeoffs.
  • Experience building scalable operating models, processes, governance mechanisms, and performance-management systems.
  • Strong analytical and financial judgment, with the ability to use data to diagnose problems, evaluate tradeoffs, develop business cases, and allocate resources.
  • Exceptional executive communication and stakeholder-management skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience integrating Trust & Safety operations following acquisitions, strategic partnerships, international expansion, or entry into new business lines.
  • Experience operationalizing regulatory or compliance requirements across complex products and global operations.
  • Experience with safety transparency reporting, regulatory reporting, audits, or other complex external accountability programs.
  • Experience using AI, automation, and advanced analytics to improve operational quality, efficiency, detection, decision-making, or customer experience.

Role Considerations

Trust & Safety work can involve sensitive subject matter. In this role, you may be exposed to descriptions, reports, or other content involving violence, sexual assault, harassment, or other potentially graphic or distressing safety incidents. You may also be asked to participate in legal proceedings (e.g. depositions), related to Lyft’s Trust & Safety practices or specific matters.

title: Senior Product Manager, Customer Care AI
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our mission is to improve people's lives with the world's best transportation. To do this, we start with our own community by creating an open, inclusive, and diverse organization.

Lyft connects people to transportation to change the way we live and get around our communities. We are looking for product managers who bring exceptional creative and analytical skills to drive forward a best in class product. Product management at Lyft leads the integration of engineering, data science, and design to achieve the company's vision for reinventing transportation. We are looking for entrepreneurial and passionate Product Managers to innovate and execute across a rapidly growing, fast paced company and industry from our San Francisco and New York offices.

The Customer Care team is at the forefront of building intelligent AI agents that transform how Lyft delivers customer support. As AI capabilities evolve rapidly, we're moving beyond traditional automation to create AI agents that can understand complex customer needs, make intelligent decisions, and resolve issues with human-level quality. This team works cross-functionally to design, deploy, and scale AI agents that handle real customer conversations and empower our human agents with more information to solve issues. They work alongside our support ops and insights teams to create exceptional experiences when our customers need help most.

Responsibilities:

  • Build and optimize AI agents that handle customer support interactions across chat and voice channels
  • Partner directly with engineering, data science, and ML teams to design agent capabilities and behaviors
  • Write, test, and refine prompt logic and conversation flows for specific customer use cases
  • Partner with support operations teams to understand workflows, pain points, and opportunities
  • Run rapid feedback loops between customer interactions and product development to continuously improve agent performance
  • Serve as the in-house expert on AI agent development, translating technical capabilities into business impact
  • Define success metrics and drive data-informed decisions to ensure optimal prioritization
  • Create an AI strategy that scales as Lyft grows

title: Security Assurance Analyst, Security and Privacy
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

Lyft connects people to transportation to change the way we live and get around our communities. Our drivers and passengers entrust Lyft with their personal information and travel details to get where they are going and expect us to keep that data safe. Lyft's Privacy and Compliance team ensures that appropriate security controls and data protections are applied to meet our compliance requirements and customer obligations We conduct security risk assessments, consult with organizational stakeholders, monitor and continuously improve Lyft's Information Security program, facilitate third-party security audits, work with engineering teams to implement, automate, and monitor security controls, develop policies, and advise on all matters related to information security assurance. We also conduct risk assessments of our third parties to ensure we understand and can mitigate any associated risk. 

We are looking for a highly motivated, organized, and detail-oriented individual to join our Privacy and Compliance team. As a senior member of this team, you will support our third party risk management program by conducting risk assessments and recommending mitigations. You will also help our Customer Trust team by completing inbound security and data protection questionnaires from potential partners and customers. 

Responsibilities:

  • Third Party Risk Assessments 
    • Review vendor or partner requests from internal stakeholders, understanding the business purpose 
    • Work with external stakeholders to collect relevant security and data protection information from third parties
    • Review the information and accurately assess and document the risk, and propose potential mitigations 
  • Security Questionnaires 
    • Draft responses to customer security questionnaires (e.g., CAIQ, SIG) and assist in the management of our external trust center (SafeBase)
  • Program Management 
    • Help senior team members in managing workflows, queues, and tools
    • Help the team track and compile reporting and metrics  

Experience:

Required

  • 1-3 years of program management experience supporting third party risk management and security compliance and assurance  
  • Knowledge of security frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, SOX ITGC, or with international privacy/security regulations such as GDPR, EU AI Act, NIS2, or other international privacy/security compliance experience
  • Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills 
  • Ability to manage a large workload and competing priorities amid resourcing constraints and tight deadlines
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills across technical, business, and executive audiences
  • Interest in leveraging AI tools or large language models (LLMs), including tools like Claude or Gemini, to automate, improve, or design compliance and assurance processes, documentation, or controls — for example AI-assisted evidence review, policy drafting, questionnaire completion, or pattern analysis across audit findings
  • Familiarity with with GRC platforms (e.g., AuditBoard CrossComply, Vanta, or Drata), Safebase, Jira, and vendor management tools
  • Knowledge of microservices SaaS product infrastructures or tech stacks a plus

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Data Science, or a related field preferred
  • Relevant certifications such as Comptia Security+, Network+, PMP, CIPP a plus

title: Software Engineer, Telematics
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

We are looking for an experienced backend software engineer to join our Road Safety & Telematics team. At Lyft, Telematics data is used to make Lyft safer by reducing the frequency and severity of accidents, which in turn also makes Lyft more affordable for riders and a better way to earn a living for drivers. The Telematics team acts as a platform team that processes petabytes of mobile sensor data — millisecond-level IMU, gyroscope, and GPS signals — through a series of DAG-based transformations and ML model inferences to detect harsh driving events and convert them into normalized risk features that other Lyft services consume.

Our technology stack runs on AWS, Kubernetes, Spark, and Apache Airflow. In this role, you'll work closely with data scientists, actuarial teams, other backend and data engineers, and product management — partnering across geos to build risk-aware products that rank and reward safe drivers, help off-board unsafe ones, notify drivers in real time, and give claims agents the tools to understand exactly what happened in a ride. You'll also be a key technical partner to our insurance team as they optimize coverage costs and provider relationships.

If you are a seasoned engineer with a passion for innovation, high-volume data pipelines, microservices, working in cross-disciplinary environments and possess the skills to ensure the ongoing maintenance and improvement of services, you will thrive on our team!

You can read about some of the products that Telematics powers in this blog post: https://www.lyft.com/blog/posts/lyfts-impact-on-road-safety

Responsibilities:

  • Be a champion of the team's safety and affordability mission, serving as a reliable source of risk insights for teams across Lyft — from driver ranking and safety rewards to accident claims resolution and insurance strategy.
  • Lead medium to large projects, ensuring end-to-end execution with a focus on high quality and reliability.
  • Work cross-functionally with Data Scientists to productionize models that turn raw sensor signals into harsh-event detection and risk features, driving the team's industry-leading innovation in this space.
  • Drive future work to reduce latency, simplify, and improve the accuracy of both our back-end and on-device models that predict accidents before they happen.
  • Actively unblock and support team members, fostering a collaborative and efficient work environment.
  • Take a lead role in the ongoing maintenance of our Telematics systems, reducing tech debt and operating costs through sensible, data-driven design decisions.
  • Collaborate with product management and leadership across geos to define and execute ambitious roadmaps for Telematics.
  • Apply the latest AI tools to boost engineering and business productivity, sharing what you learn with the team.
  • Utilize your expertise in Python, AWS, Spark, SQL (Databricks/Presto), etc. to deliver robust and scalable solutions.
  • Participate in our team's on-call rotations, respond to incidents, and support other teams in mitigating customer-impacting events.

Experience:

  • 4+ years of software engineering industry experience
  • Experience in backend software development of large-scale distributed systems
  • Experience and/or interest in running large batch processing jobs with Spark or other large scale compute architectures
  • Experience and/or interest in Library development
  • Experience and/or interest in serving, versioning, monitoring ML models in production environments
  • Experience defining API schemas and developing backend services in a microservices environment
  • Experience with S3, Spark, Presto, Parquet, Databricks
  • You're a great communicator, and can advocate for your proposals while also empathizing with your cross-functional teammates' goals and priorities
  • You collaborate well with a geographically distributed team

title: Ingénieur(e) en Micrologiciel, LUS
descriptionHtml:
Chez Lyft, notre mission est de servir et de connecter. Nous y parvenons en favorisant un environnement de travail où chacun trouve sa place et a la possibilité de s'épanouir.

Lyft Urban Solutions fournit les systèmes de vélos et de trottinettes en libre-service qui permettent à des millions de personnes de se déplacer dans plus de 60 villes à travers le monde. Nous avons créé le premier système de vélos en libre-service automatisé d'Amérique du Nord et restons à la pointe de la révolution de la micromobilité. Nos systèmes sont présents partout dans le monde : de Citi Bike à New York à BIXI à Montréal, en passant par Divvy à Chicago, Capital Bikeshare à Washington D.C., et des systèmes emblématiques à Austin, Barcelone, Bogota, Boston, Buenos Aires, Columbus, Detroit, Dubaï, Londres, Madrid, Mexico, Monaco, Pittsburgh, Portland, Rio de Janeiro, San Francisco, Toronto et bien d'autres villes.

Nous ne sommes pas de simples fournisseurs de technologies : nous exploitons ces systèmes, en développant les logiciels, le matériel et les opérations qui permettent à la micromobilité urbaine de fonctionner à grande échelle.

Prêt à façonner la façon dont des millions de personnes se déplacent chaque jour dans leurs villes ?

Le rôle d'ingénieur(e) en micrologiciel chez Lyft Urban Solutions (LUS) est crucial pour le développement et la livraison des solutions matérielles de micromobilité de Lyft, qui incluent les vélos électriques, les trottinettes, les batteries et les stations. Nous recherchons un(e) ingénieur(e) en micrologiciel possédant des compétences techniques exceptionnelles pour contribuer aux programmes d'introduction de nouveaux produits (NPI) et de durabilité de la flotte, qui ajoutent de la valeur aux villes du monde entier utilisant nos produits. Les ingénieur(e)s en micrologiciel chez Lyft collaborent étroitement avec les équipes de matériel, des opérations et de fabrication. Ce rôle exige donc une solide expertise technique, des compétences en leadership et en communication. Ce sont des résolveurs de problèmes proactifs qui font avancer les initiatives, assurant le succès de livraisons clés qui ont un impact significatif sur l'entreprise.

Responsabilités:

  • Développer des fonctionnalités pour les systèmes embarqués de notre gamme de produits de micromobilité (véhicules, stations (dock), outils internes).
  • Collaborer avec les équipes multifonctionnelles pour prototyper, développer et mettre en production notre prochaine génération de produits de mobilité de classe mondiale.
  • Travailler sur des améliorations et des mises à jour pour bonifier l'expérience globale sur les produits existants.

Expérience:

  • Baccalauréat en informatique ou dans un domaine connexe.
  • Plus de 5 ans d'expérience en développement C/C++ pour les systèmes embarqués.
  • Familiarité avec l'utilisation de Python pour le scripting et les tests automatisés.
  • Expérience avec un système d'exploitation en temps réel embarqué (FreeRTOS, ThreadX, etc.).
  • Compréhension des concepts de base des systèmes d'exploitation (gestion de la mémoire, ordonnancement, threads, interruptions).
  • Familiarité avec la gamme de processeurs ARM Cortex-M.
  • Expérience pratique dans la mise en service électrique et le débogage.
  • Solides compétences en débogage de systèmes embarqués, incluant l'utilisation de sondes de débogage, d'analyseurs de signaux, d'oscilloscopes et d'analyseurs de puissance.
  • Expérience dans la traduction des besoins des produits en échéanciers réalisables.
  • Solides compétences en communication pour expliquer les approches techniques et partager l'avancement et les risques avec des publics non techniques.
  • Solide compréhension des concepts de systèmes distribués.

title: Legal Operations Specialist
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

We are looking for a detail-driven Legal Billing Specialist to join our growing Legal Operations Team. In this role, you will own the day-to-day of outside counsel and vendor billing across our matter management and eBilling platforms—reviewing invoices, enforcing our Outside Counsel Guidelines and negotiated fee arrangements, and keeping our legal spend accurate, compliant, and on time. The ideal candidate is tech-savvy, numbers-oriented, and thrives under recurring billing deadlines, bringing a collaborative and transparent approach to partnering with attorneys, law firms, and Finance. This is a billing-focused role that also supports the broader Legal Operations function.

Responsibilities:

  • Prepare, review, and process outside counsel and vendor invoices; audit prebills and invoices, and flag rate errors, block-billing, math discrepancies, and billing-guideline violations before approval.
  • Manage the day-to-day operation of the eBilling and matter management platform (Onit), including invoice intake, LEDES processing, rejections and appeals, accruals, and international / AP invoice processing.
  • Enforce compliance with Lyft’s Outside Counsel Guidelines (OCG) and negotiated fee and alternative fee arrangements (AFAs); process write-offs, write-downs, and adjustments with clear documentation and audit trail.
  • Manage timekeeper and billing-rate submissions and approvals; maintain accurate rate cards, matter budgets, and phase/task coding across the portfolio.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for billing inquiries and disputes; resolve discrepancies promptly by partnering with attorneys, law firms, and support staff.
  • Partner closely with the Legal Operations eBilling Lead and with Finance / Accounts Payable on accruals, month- and quarter-end close, reconciliation, and payment status.
  • Onboard outside counsel and vendors to our billing program, including engagement letters, budgets, and billing-guideline acknowledgment.
  • Develop and iterate on spend metrics, dashboards, and benchmarking through data analytics to measure efficiency, surface trends, and identify cost-savings opportunities.
  • Codify billing workflows into playbooks and intake templates; support platform efficiencies, configuration, testing, and report validation.
  • Support broader Legal Operations initiatives and process improvements as needed.

Experience:

  • A bachelor’s degree or higher preferred; coursework or a background in accounting, finance, or business administration is a plus.
  • At least 2+ years of legal billing or eBilling experience in an in-house legal department, law firm, or both.
  • Hands-on experience with an eBilling / matter management platform—Onit, Legal Tracker, Brightflag —and familiarity with LEDES invoice formats.
  • Working knowledge of outside counsel billing guidelines, alternative fee arrangements, rate structures, and accruals.
  • Strong Excel and analytical skills, with an eye for accuracy in high-volume, deadline-driven billing cycles.
  • Understanding of financial management principles and process-improvement experience.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to build relationships across the business and with external law firms at all levels.
  • A proactive, entrepreneurial approach—recognizing needs, anticipating issues, and following through with a strong sense of ownership.
  • Comfortable with new challenges and frequent change, with the ability to manage several priorities simultaneously.
  • Experience with tools such as Ironclad, Evisort, Tonkean, and Google Suite is a plus.

Benefits:

  • Great medical, dental, and vision insurance options with additional programs available when enrolled
  • Mental health benefits
  • Family building benefits
  • Child care and pet benefits
  • 401(k) plan with company match to help save for your future
  • In addition to 12 observed holidays, salaried team members have discretionary paid time off, hourly team members have 15 days paid time off
  • 18 weeks of paid parental leave. Biological, adoptive, and foster parents are all eligible
  • Subsidized commuter benefits
  • Monthly Lyft credits and complimentary Lyft Pink membership

title: Firmware Engineering Manager, Lyft Urban Solutions
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

Lyft Urban Solutions powers the bike-sharing and scooter-sharing systems that move millions of people in over 60 cities worldwide. We built North America's first automated bike-share system and continue to lead the micromobility revolution. Our systems operate globally - from Citi Bike in New York to BIXI in Montreal, Divvy in Chicago, Capital Bikeshare in DC, and iconic systems in Austin, Barcelona, Bogota, Boston, Buenos Aires, Columbus, Detroit, Dubai, London, Madrid, Mexico City, Monaco, Pittsburgh, Portland, Rio de Janeiro, San Francisco, Toronto, and beyond.

We're not just technology providers - we operate these systems, building the software, hardware, and operations that make urban micromobility work at scale.

Ready to shape how millions of people move through their cities every day?

The Lyft Urban Solutions (LUS) Firmware Engineering Manager role is central to the development and delivery of Lyft's micromobility hardware offerings, including e-bikes, scooters, batteries, charging stations, and more! We are looking for a Firmware Engineering Manager who combines deep technical expertise in embedded systems with strong people leadership to grow and guide a team of firmware engineers. This person will drive the technical roadmap for New Product Introduction (NPI) and fleet sustainability programs, while building the team, processes, and technical culture needed to deliver safe, reliable, and field-proven firmware at scale across the cities that rely on our products. Firmware Engineering Managers at Lyft partner closely with hardware, software, product, data science, manufacturing, operations, and compliance teams, and are expected to bring strong technical judgment, organizational leadership, and clear communication to every level of the business.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead, mentor, and grow a team of firmware engineers building embedded software across Lyft's micromobility product line — e-bikes, scooters, batteries, docks, and charging infrastructure
  • Set technical direction and architecture for core firmware systems — IoT, powertrain, battery management, and docking/charging infrastructure — including safety-critical fault handling
  • Own the OTA update and fleet operations strategy: secure, staged rollout pipelines, remote diagnostics, and field recovery mechanisms that reduce on-site service visits and fleet downtime across a globally distributed fleet
  • Partner with cross-functional stakeholders — hardware, software, product, data science, manufacturing, operations, and compliance teams — to prototype, develop, and ship the next generation of world-class mobility products
  • Own team planning: roadmapping, sprint/release planning, staffing, hiring, and performance management, translating ambiguous product needs into clear, actionable schedules and deliverables
  • Drive continuous improvement of existing fielded products, prioritizing reliability, safety, and rider/operator experience
  • Represent the firmware team in regulatory and safety certification efforts (e.g., UL 2849/2271, EN 18031, and RED/CRA), ensuring firmware practices meet applicable standards
  • Build and maintain engineering rigor: CI/CD pipelines, automated Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing, code review standards, and on-call/incident response processes for fielded fleets
  • Communicate technical risk, tradeoffs, and progress clearly to both engineering peers and non-technical stakeholders and leadership
  • Support career development of direct reports and contribute to broader engineering org initiatives (technical ladders, succession planning, cross-team standards)

Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related field
  • 8+ years developing in C/C++ for embedded systems, including 2+ years directly managing or formally leading firmware/embedded engineers
  • Proven experience translating product and business needs into team roadmaps, staffing plans, and actionable schedules
  • Deep understanding of embedded real-time operating systems (FreeRTOS, ThreadX, etc.) and low-level OS concepts (memory management, scheduling, threads, interrupts)
  • Hands-on background with ARM Cortex-M processors, electrical bring-up, and embedded debugging (debug probes, signal analyzers, oscilloscopes, power analyzers)
  • Working knowledge of IoT, motor control, battery management systems (BMS), and CAN bus protocols in the context of electric vehicles or similar hardware products
  • Experience with OTA update systems and remote fleet diagnostics for distributed hardware deployments
  • Familiarity with modern firmware development practices — CI/CD pipelines, automated HIL test infrastructure — and openness to modern systems languages (e.g., Rust) alongside C/C++
  • Familiarity with functional safety and regulatory frameworks relevant to connected hardware (e.g., ISO 26262, MISRA C, EN 18031, UL standards)
  • Strong track record of cross-functional collaboration with hardware, software, product, data science, manufacturing, operations, and compliance teams on NPI and sustaining engineering programs
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to articulate technical strategy and risk to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Demonstrated ability to build inclusive, high-performing engineering teams and develop engineers' careers

title: Senior AI Software Engineer, Risk - Insurance Claims Management
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

The Risk Tech engineering organization is committed to tangibly reducing accident frequency, saving lives, and managing costs to enhance the safety and affordability of rides.

Claim Management is a core financial function for Lyft. Each claim touches complex workflows, multiple stakeholders, sensitive data, financial reserves, regulatory processes, and significant financial liabilities.

This role offers the opportunity to define a leading claims management system for the industry. Our vision is to establish a single, Unified Risk Platform where comprehensive claims workflows across all business lines are efficiently administered, communications are consolidated, and data is structured to facilitate data-driven insights and decisions.

This enables cost-efficient claims operations, mitigates risks and expenses as Lyft scales, and ensures people receive assistance proactively and accurately.

We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer to contribute to the technical direction, drive architectural decisions, and lead the development of a highly reliable, scalable, and intelligent Risk Management Information System that powers our insurance platform. You will collaborate with passionate colleagues from Engineering, Data Science, Product and Claim Operations to deliver end-to-end solutions.

 Responsibilities:

  • Define and drive the long-term technical roadmap for claims management systems, aligning priorities with Product, Claim Operations, Data Science, and other stakeholders.
  • Provide architectural leadership, make informed design tradeoffs, and guide strategic decisions across multiple engineering teams.
  • Understand claim handling workflows, identify bottlenecks and multiply their productivity by driving platform innovations and resolving pain points with AI automation solutions
  • Deliver scalable, reliable, high quality and well-tested solutions and code.
  • Collaborate closely with Lyft internal teams and external insurance partners to ensure technical alignment and scalable integrations.

Experience:

  • 6+ years of professional experience building scalable distributed systems with high availability, observability and reliability requirements.
  • Proven ability to build end-to-end products and platforms, collaborating effectively with various stakeholders e.g. Backend, Frontend, Data Engineering, Data Science, Claim Operations, and Product teams.
  • Strong ability to reason about tradeoffs in system design, architecture, domain modeling, and operational cost.
  • Experience developing AI features using multimodal LLMs, RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, and other relevant AI frameworks.
  • Experience driving AI adoption or AI automation tools to enhance development efficiency
  • Experience improving performance with robust evals,agent tracing tools, fine-tuning LLMs, optimizing RAG pipelines and implementing feedback loops.

descriptionHtml:

title: Industrialization Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. Lyft Urban Solutions designs, builds, and operates bikeshare systems in more than 50 cities worldwide, including New York, Chicago, London, Barcelona, Mexico City, Rio de Janeiro, and Montréal. Our Longueuil facility is the birthplace of BIXI, North America's first automated bikeshare system, and today builds the bikes and stations behind some of the world's largest bikeshare networks.

We are looking for an Industrialization Engineer Intern to join our Manufacturing & Quality Engineering team at our Longueuil factory. You will work on the production floor with assembly, warehouse, and quality teams to make our processes faster, safer, and more consistent. You will also be part of a global team that supports factories and suppliers across North America and Asia.

Responsibilities:

  • Map current-state material flow and factory/warehouse layout, then propose improvements that reduce waste and operator travel.
  • Run cycle time studies across assembly and warehouse operations to find bottlenecks and improve throughput and line balance.
  • Audit SOP adherence on the floor, identify gaps, and drive corrective actions or SOP updates.
  • Lead 5S audits and implement visual controls and workplace organization standards.
  • Build dashboards that track throughput, WIP, cycle time, and SOP compliance, and turn the data into recommendations.
  • Create visual work instructions, standard work sheets, and layout drawings to support operator training.
  • Support continuous improvement projects, including ergonomic assessments, workstation redesign, and tooling and fixture improvements.
  • Prepare processes for engineering changes (ECOs) and new product introductions, including layout changes and workstation validation.
  • Partner with Quality to investigate production defects and contribute to root cause analysis and PFMEA updates.

  • Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program in Industrial, Manufacturing, or Mechanical Engineering, or a related field, at a Canadian university, graduating between December 2027 and summer 2028 (required). Master's students who worked between degrees should have less than 2 years of full-time experience.
  • Professional proficiency in French and English, written and spoken (required)
  • Working knowledge of lean manufacturing principles (JIT, standard work, 5S, value stream mapping)

title: Stagiaire en ingénierie d'industrialisation (été 2027)
descriptionHtml:
Chez Lyft, notre raison d'être est de servir et de connecter. Lyft Urban Solutions conçoit, fabrique et exploite des systèmes de vélopartage dans plus de 50 villes à travers le monde, dont New York, Chicago, Londres, Barcelone, Mexico, Rio de Janeiro et Montréal. Notre usine de Longueuil est le berceau de BIXI, le premier système de vélopartage automatisé en Amérique du Nord, et fabrique aujourd'hui les vélos et les stations de certains des plus grands réseaux de vélopartage au monde.

Nous recherchons un ou une stagiaire en ingénierie d'industrialisation pour se joindre à notre équipe Ingénierie de la fabrication et de la qualité (Manufacturing & Quality Engineering) à notre usine de Longueuil. Vous travaillerez sur le plancher de production avec les équipes d'assemblage, d'entrepôt et de qualité afin de rendre nos procédés plus rapides, plus sécuritaires et plus constants. Vous ferez également partie d'une équipe mondiale qui soutient des usines et des fournisseurs en Amérique du Nord et en Asie.

Responsabilités :

  • Cartographier le flux de matières et l'aménagement actuel de l'usine et de l'entrepôt, puis proposer des améliorations pour réduire le gaspillage et les déplacements des opérateurs.
  • Réaliser des études de temps de cycle pour les opérations d'assemblage et d'entrepôt afin de repérer les goulots d'étranglement et d'améliorer le débit et l'équilibrage des lignes.
  • Auditer le respect des instructions d’assemblage sur le plancher, cerner les écarts et piloter les mesures correctives ou les mises à jour des instructions d’assemblage.
  • Diriger les audits 5S et mettre en place des contrôles visuels et des normes d'organisation du milieu de travail.
  • Concevoir des tableaux de bord pour suivre le débit, les encours, les temps de cycle et le respect des d’assemblage , et transformer les données en recommandations.
  • Créer des instructions de travail visuelles, des fiches de travail standardisées.
  • Contribuer à des projets d'amélioration continue, notamment des évaluations ergonomiques, la reconfiguration de postes de travail et l'amélioration d'outillages et de gabarits.
  • Préparer les procédés en vue des modifications techniques (ECO) et des lancements de nouveaux produits, y compris les changements d'aménagement et la validation des postes de travail.
  • Collaborer avec l'équipe Qualité pour enquêter sur les défauts de production et contribuer à l'analyse des causes profondes et à la mise à jour des risques par procédé (PFMEA).

Expérience :

  • Être inscrit ou inscrite à un programme de baccalauréat ou de maîtrise en génie industriel, en génie mécanique ou dans un domaine connexe dans une université canadienne, avec une fin d'études prévue entre décembre 2027 et l'été 2028 (obligatoire). Les personnes à la maîtrise ayant travaillé entre leurs deux programmes doivent cumuler moins de 2 ans d'expérience à temps plein.
  • Maîtrise professionnelle du français et de l'anglais, à l'écrit comme à l'oral (obligatoire)
  • Connaissance pratique des principes de production allégée (juste-à-temps, travail standardisé, 5S, cartographie de la chaîne de valeur)
  • Expérience avec AutoCAD ou un logiciel de CAO similaire pour la conception d'aménagements
  • Solides compétences analytiques et souci du détail
  • Aisance dans un environnement au rythme soutenu, avec la capacité de gérer plusieurs priorités selon l'évolution des besoins sur le plancher
  • Un stage ou un stage coopératif antérieur en fabrication, en opérations ou en qualité constitue un atout
  • Une expérience avec Mode, Hex, Tableau ou Power BI constitue un atout, tout comme la connaissance de SQL ou de Python
  • La connaissance de Jira ou d'outils de gestion de billets similaires constitue un atout
  • La connaissance des systèmes PLM ou des processus de modification technique constitue un atou

title: PhD Machine Learning Software Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

With over half a billion rides and counting, Lyft is solving hard problems in a flourishing domain with a lot of data and creative solutions in Marketplace, Mapping, Fraud, Growth and beyond. We're actively building the next-generation Machine Learning (ML) platform for low-cost, ultra-immersive transportation to improve people’s lives using modern ML with petabyte-scale data. Our Machine Learning Engineers are excited to work on these challenging problems and redefine solutions to directly impact various aspects of Lyft's primary business.

As a PhD Machine Learning Engineer Intern on our Applied AI team, you'll take on an open research problem tied to product experiences used by millions of riders. Working closely with a Staff ML Engineer mentor, you'll scope the problem, develop and evaluate new methods on real data, and take the work far enough that it can be shared with the research community, with the goal of a paper submission to a top ML venue.

If you are a PhD student who enjoys turning open-ended research questions into working systems, and you want your research to be tested against real users and real data, this opportunity is for you!

Responsibilities:

  • Own a research project from start to finish: frame the problem, review related work, propose new methods, and design rigorous offline and online evaluations
  • Design, build, train and test ML models in areas such as reinforcement learning, sequential decision-making, personalization
  • Write production-quality code that turns research prototypes into working pipelines on Lyft's data and ML infrastructure
  • Partner with Product Managers, Data Scientists, and fellow ML Engineers to frame research questions within the business context
  • Analyze experimental and observational data, and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Write up results for publication at a peer-reviewed venue, with support from your mentor and the team
  • Participate in code and spec reviews to ensure code quality and distribute knowledge

Experience:

  • Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field, and returning to your program after the internship, with a graduation date between December 2027 and Summer 2028 (required)
  • A track record of ML research, shown through publications, preprints, or substantial research projects
  • Strong foundation in reinforcement learning and sequential decision making, especially problems with delayed or long-horizon rewards
  • Solid grounding in both causal inference and counterfactual evaluation
  • Good understanding of ML libraries like PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX

title: VP, People
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

Lyft is in a defining moment: accelerating growth, expanding internationally, and building the world's leading hybrid rideshare network. How we build, organize, and lead our people will determine how well we get there. As Vice President, People, you will help drive the business forward through the strength of our people strategy, serving as a right hand to our Chief People Officer and a trusted advisor to Lyft's executive leadership team. This is a high-impact role for a seasoned people executive who operates at altitude and on the ground in equal measure, thrives in fast-paced, dynamic environments, and is energized by the chance to own some of the most complex and consequential work in the function.

Reporting to the Chief People Officer, you will lead the People Business Partner organization, own workforce planning for the enterprise, and drive the human capital strategy behind Lyft's M&A activity from diligence through integration. You'll partner directly with the executive leadership team, represent the People function in cross-functional forums, and shape the org design, structure and ways of working that will carry Lyft into its next chapter. You'll anticipate challenges, help leaders look around corners, and bring forward-thinking solutions to keep Lyft's workforce agile, engaged, and ready for the future while shaping how the People function itself grows from here.

Join us and help shape the future of work at one of the most mission-driven, people-focused companies redefining mobility.

Responsibilities:

Executive Partnership & People Strategy

  • Partner directly with the Chief People Officer and executive leadership team on the people strategy behind Lyft's most significant business decisions, acting as a trusted advisor and bringing best-in-class practices to enable growth.

People Business Partnering & Org Leadership

  • Own the Global People Business Partner function (team of 14) end to end across Lyft's global footprint — strategy, structure, and team leadership — driving organizational effectiveness and modernizing how the function delivers value at scale across every market, region, and legal entity we operate in. Get into the details when it matters — from a thorny org design problem to a retention conversation with a critical hire.
  • Anticipate workforce challenges and guide leaders through complex organizational change with empathy and strategic foresight
  • Shape scalable team structures and influence how Lyft builds leadership pipelines, attracts, develops, and retains top talent across the company
  • Lead, empower, and develop a team of high-performing People Business Partners, fostering a culture of strategic impact, continuous growth, and bench strength for the function's next generation of leaders

M&A Human Capital

  • Lead the human capital workstream for Lyft's international M&A activity, including cultural and talent due diligence, retention-risk assessment, org design and integration planning, comp and benefits harmonization, and Day 1 readiness for newly acquired teams — including cross-border and works-council considerations. You're as comfortable running the details of a deal integration as you are advising the executive team on strategy.

Workforce Planning & Future of Work

  • Own enterprise workforce planning in partnership with Finance — multi-year headcount and skills planning, scenario and contingency planning, and workforce analytics that inform where and how Lyft invests in talent globally. 
  • Partner with Team Member Experience and Tech to help our people and teams grow alongside new tools and technology; from emerging skills needs to how we work together most effectively.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner closely with other Centers of Excellence (Talent Acquisition, Team Member Experience, Total Rewards, People Operations, Culture & Belonging) and with Legal to enable programs that create meaningful business impact
  • Partner with People Systems & Operations to modernize team member self-service capabilities through technology and automation, and drive adoption across the business

title: Sr. Manager, GTM Strategy & Sales Packaging
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

Lyft Ads gives brands a unique way to reach consumers during high-intent moments: on their way to concerts, games, nights out, and everyday destinations. In this role, you'll set the strategy behind how we bring those moments to market, arm our sellers to win, and connect advertisers with millions of riders across the country.

Lyft Ads is looking for a Senior Manager of Sales Packaging & Go-to-Market Strategy to build and lead the function that turns ridership data, cultural moments, and product capabilities into the packages our sales team sells every day. This is a strategic leadership role: you'll set the packaging and pricing agenda for the full Lyft Ads portfolio, build the go-to-market motions behind our biggest revenue moments, and give sellers the stories, structure, and pricing tools they need to win.

You are a builder. You operate comfortably at the intersection of strategy and execution, and you have a track record of driving commercial outcomes in ambiguous, fast-moving environments. You bring a POV to partnership and packaging conversations, and you know how to align internal and external stakeholders around a shared vision. You are energized by the challenge of taking a scaled, high-growth advertising business and making it even better: more differentiated, more efficient, and more impactful for the brands and agencies that invest with Lyft Ads.

You'll operate at the intersection of data, product, pricing, creative, and sales, and you'll be expected to bring an independent point of view on where Lyft Ads should show up, what we should charge, and how we package multi-product solutions with measurement built in. This role owns and manages the Lyft Ads Studio team, sits at the table with Sales leadership, and works in close partnership with Data Science, Finance, Product Marketing, Product, and cross-functional leadership across the business.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the sales packaging strategy for Lyft Ads' full suite of on- and off-platform advertising solutions, building differentiated packages that map to advertiser objectives and buying behavior
  • Set the vision and calendar for tentpole and cultural-moment packaging (Super Bowl, March Madness, Women’s World Cup, Coachella, Formula 1, SXSW, Halloween, Valentine's Day, New Year's Eve), using ridership and audience data to identify where and when advertisers should show up
  • Craft the go-to-market narratives behind each package, from initial data-driven thesis to the story sellers use in market, in partnership with Product Marketing and Lyft Ads Studio
  • Formulate pricing and deal economics for sponsorships, tentpole packages, and multi-product bundles, balancing revenue optimization with competitive positioning and advertiser value
  • Build multi-product solutions that combine packaging with measurement frameworks, giving advertisers a clear read on performance and giving sellers proof points to close
  • Partner with Sales, Data Science, and Finance to model package performance, set pricing guardrails, and build scalable frameworks for both direct IO and programmatic deal structures
  • Develop audience-segmented packaging for key verticals (CPG, QSR, Auto, Financial Services, Travel) to sharpen sales conversations by category
  • Own the GTM materials that arm the field: one-sheets, rate cards, media plans, packaging guides, and sales playbooks
  • Establish a feedback loop between field sales and the packaging/pricing function so offerings stay relevant, competitive, and commercially viable

title: AV Program Manager
descriptionHtml:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

Flexdrive, Lyft's wholly-owned fleet management subsidiary, is undergoing a transformational shift from traditional rideshare fleet operations to autonomous vehicle fleet ownership and operations. We are seeking an AV Program Manager to help drive the cross-functional operating plan that will prepare Flexdrive to receive, staff, and operate AV fleets at scale domestically and abroad.

This role supports the operational backbone of Flexdrive's AV readiness initiative. You will maintain the program timeline, coordinate cross-functional workstreams spanning infrastructure, people, fleet operations, treasury, legal, and finance, and help ensure that requirements are tracked, dependencies are surfaced, and deployment milestones are met. You will work closely with workstream leads across Operations, Strategy, Infrastructure, Finance,  Legal, Analytics, and People.

If you thrive in ambiguity, can bring structure to complex multi-workstream programs, and have a bias toward action, this role is for you.

Responsibilities:

1. Program Planning & Execution

  • Maintain the program timeline for Flexdrive AV Operating Readiness, tracking deliverables and dependencies across workstreams: Strategic Planning, Infrastructure, Analytics, People, Fleet Operations, Treasury, Finance, and Legal.
  • Maintain the program's RAID log (Risks, Assumptions, Issues, Dependencies), surfacing cross-functional blockers with clear context for escalation.
  • Support weekly leadership syncs and monthly deep-dive reviews, including preparation, presentation and follow-through.

2. Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Serve as a connection point between workstream leads, helping ensure infrastructure timelines align with hiring plans, capital deployment schedules match construction milestones, and fleet operations readiness tracks to vehicle delivery dates.
  • Act as the central hub across cross-functional internal teams supporting the program; drive alignment on priorities and decisions, escalate issues with the right context, and be accountable for resolution 
  • Coordinate with People and Operations to help sequence hiring, training, and certification programs ahead of vehicle arrivals.
  • Work with FP&A and Treasury to track investment spend against the capital deployment schedule and flag variance early.

3. Stakeholder Communication & Reporting

  • Build and deliver clear status reporting to program leadership and workstream stakeholders.
  • Ensure cross-functional stakeholders stay aligned on expectations, deliverables, and timelines throughout the program.
  • Maintain market readiness scorecards that provide visibility into each market's progress against deployment milestones.
  • Create and maintain program documentation including decision logs, meeting notes, and workstream status trackers.

4. Process Support & Operational Excellence

  • Help design and implement the program management operating model for AV readiness
